news.head: A winter storm shuts down Illinois
news.body: A foot of snow and sheets of ice have closed schools and highways. Utility crews are working to restore power.

news.head: A heat dome bakes the South
news.body: Cities from Phoenix to Atlanta are setting records, and cooling centers are full.

news.head: White House: the president has a cold and is working from the residence

news.body: Everyone seems to be talking about the same show, and the actors are suddenly famous.

news.head: Shapiro visits Texas
Shapiro visits Texas
The Super Bowl is the most-watched broadcast of the year
news.body: Parties across the country, and advertisers paying record sums for a few seconds of airtime.

news.head: A county fair in Nevada draws record crowds
news.body: Prize hogs, pie contests and a Ferris wheel. Organizers say it was the best fair in memory.

news.head: Budget office: the Chips and China Act will cost $16 billion over ten years
news.body: Little effect on the size of the economy; it will cost $16 billion over ten years.

Sports betting apps are everywhere
news.body: Millions of Americans now bet on games from their phones. Counselors say calls to gambling hotlines are up.

news.head: A new hospital opens in Delaware
news.body: The hospital will serve a rural region where the nearest emergency room was more than an hour away.

news.head: A new generation of weight-loss drugs becomes a pill
news.body: Millions of Americans are taking the drugs, and food companies are reporting a drop in snack sales.

news.head: Bitter cold grips the northern states
news.body: Temperatures fell below zero from Montana to Maine. Shelters opened extra beds.

news.head: AI chatbots move into offices and classrooms
news.body: Companies are using AI to write code and answer customers. Schools are rewriting their rules on homework.

news.head: A singer from Louisiana has the number one song in the country
news.body: The young singer recorded it in a small studio. Now it's on every radio.

news.head: A new shopping center opens outside Connecticut's biggest city
news.body: The developer says it will be the region's largest, with department stores and hundreds of shops.

news.head: Veterans return to a quieter country
news.body: With no war on, veterans in Iowa are going back to school and starting businesses.

news.head: Self-driving trucks begin hauling freight on the interstates
news.body: The first driverless trucks are running on highways in the Southwest. The Teamsters say they're a threat to millions of jobs.

news.head: Data centers strain the grid in Virginia
news.body: A new AI campus will use as much power as a city of a million people. Utilities are asking customers to pay for new power plants.

news.head: Shapiro visits Texas
Scientists in West Virginia report a promising cancer treatment
news.body: Early trials show tumors shrinking in some patients. Researchers caution that more study is needed.

news.head: A downtown in Ohio comes back to life
news.body: Old warehouses are now apartments, restaurants and breweries.

news.head: A community in Colorado rallies after a flood
news.body: Volunteers are filling sandbags and gutting homes. Churches are serving meals around the clock.

news.head: Spring floods along the rivers of California
news.body: Melting snow and heavy rain have pushed rivers over their banks. Families are moving to higher ground.

news.head: Shapiro visits Florida

news.head: March Madness: an underdog shocks a top seed
